en: A small memorial candle burning in a tall glass on a shelf at home beside a closed holy book and a tzedakah box, soft evening light from a window. No people, no letters.
A frightened boy with a kippa hiding behind a sofa in a living room, peeking out with scared trembling eyes, as if afraid of someone coming. Only the one boy.

At a kitchen table, a boy with a kippa pointing his finger and arguing loudly with his father with a kippa, shaking his head as if saying 'you are wrong'; the father looks surprised and hurt. No speech bubbles.
A seder table at night with matza and haggadot, and in its center a large ornate silver cup full of red wine; the front door of the room stands open. No people.
A boy with a kippa proudly handing his father with a kippa a huge, very expensive-looking wrapped gift box with a golden ribbon, a shopping bag from a fancy store beside him.

A calm living room: a man with a kippa sitting on a LOW stool, and two men with kippot sitting on regular chairs facing him, talking gently and quietly; a bookshelf of holy books behind. Serious and warm, NOT heavy sadness, no crying. Only men.

A boy with a kippa waiting at a window at evening, calm and smiling; above his head a soft thought cloud shows his father with a kippa helping an old man with a kippa change a flat car tire on the road. No text.
A man with a kippa and a white tallit standing in a synagogue and holding up a silver cup of red wine, reciting a blessing with eyes on the cup. Only men.
